titleEn: Blow Out, and the Reeds Sway!

pages.text: "Show me your shell! I want to see too!" Beside the dry reeds on the bank path, Pongi pulled her brother's paw. He turned his back and hid the shell. Pongi wanted to look inside just once.
"If you won't show me, then fine!" Pongi stamped and shouted. "No," said her brother. He hugged the shell tighter and stepped backward. Only the tied-up boat rocked by the water.
After shouting, Pongi's heart was pounding. Her brother had slipped behind the reeds. The path was quiet. Pongi let both paws hang down. She felt upset.
Mom, wearing her headscarf, sat on the path and put a paw on Pongi's back. "Something hot rushed up in your chest, didn't it?" Pongi nodded. "That's anger. Anger comes for a little while, then goes."

"How do I send it away?" asked Pongi. Mom pointed to the reeds. "Breathe in through your nose, tummy out! Breathe out through your mouth, strong enough to bend the reeds!" Pongi stood right in front of them.

In through her nose, and Pongi's tummy rounded out. Out through her mouth, whooo! The dry reeds slowly bent to one side. "Blow out, and the reeds sway!" Mom sang. The heat in Pongi's chest slowly cooled.
Pongi stood in front of her brother behind the reeds. "I'm sorry I shouted. My chest felt hot. It's all gone now." She thumped her tail. "Blow out, and the reeds sway!"
Her brother opened the shell a little to show Pongi. Inside, one little stone sparkled. "Sis," he said. "Pretty!" Pongi's mouth turned up in a big smile.

On the bank path, her brother quickly hid the shell again. Pongi's chest grew hot again. She breathed in through her nose, then out through her mouth, bending the reeds! "One, tummy out! Two, blow out! Three, reeds sway!"

Mom stroked Pongi's back slowly, right down to her tail tip. "All the heat has gone!" When anger comes, a big breath helps it slowly go. Pongi put a paw on her brother's shoulder and called, "Blow out, and the reeds sway!"
